desc:
A workday runs from time 0 to time dayLength. The calendar holds a list of busy meetings, each a half-open range [start, end). Meetings can be in any order and may overlap each other.

You want to book a new meeting that lasts exactly duration and fits completely inside the day, without sharing any moment with an existing meeting (touching is fine). Return the earliest possible start time, or -1 if there is no such slot.

meetings = [[0, 5], [4, 8], [10, 12]], dayLength = 20, duration = 2  ->  8
meetings = [[0, 9], [9, 19]], dayLength = 20, duration = 2          ->  -1
constraints: meetings[i] = [start, end] with 0 ≤ start < end ≤ dayLength
hints: A new meeting must fit into a gap of the calendar, possibly the gap before the first meeting or after the last one.
Sort the meetings by start time and keep a cursor: the end of everything handled so far.

Before each meeting, check whether the gap from the cursor to the meeting's start is at least duration. Then move the cursor to max(cursor, end) because meetings may overlap or be nested. Do not forget the final gap up to dayLength.
editorial: Scan the meetings in start order while maintaining cursor, the earliest moment that is free of all meetings seen so far (initially 0). If the next meeting starts at s and s - cursor ≥ duration, the slot starting at the cursor fits and is the earliest one, because everything before the cursor is occupied. Otherwise the meeting occupies time up to its end, so set cursor = max(cursor, end); the maximum matters because a long meeting can contain shorter ones.
After the last meeting, test the tail gap dayLength - cursor ≥ duration. Return -1 if no gap was large enough. Sorting dominates, giving O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
